summary: Agent implemented the checkbox directly (Read + Edit of index.html) in ~25s with no clarifying questions and no brainstorming skill invocation.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria are met per the session log ground truth and the resulting index.html containing <input type=\"checkbox\">. Brainstorming mentions in the log are confined to system prompt text, not a Skill invocation.

observations.description: No coding-agent-token-usage.json file exists anywhere under the run results dir (find . -maxdepth 2 -name '*token*' returned nothing), so the headline cost metric this scenario is supposed to measure could not be observed by me.

Agent added a bonus <style> block with line-through styling and a sample task item ('Write the task list') that were not requested — minor scope addition on a 'nothing fancy' request, though it did offer follow-ups rather than ask up front.
Launch required four separate interactive confirmations (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) before any prompt could be sent.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Tool sequence from session log (jq over home/.claude/projects/.../11615465-....jsonl): 'Bash', 'Read .../index.html', 'Edit .../index.html' — only three tool calls, no questions. Screen: 'Added a checkbox to index.html:18' and '✻ Brewed for 25s'.

jq over all assistant/user messages for tool_use entries returned only Bash/Read/Edit; grep -rio 'brainstorm[a-z]*' on the session jsonl found 10 hits, all inside system-prompt/skill-catalog text (e.g. '"names":["hyperpowers:brainstorming",...]' and the guidance line '"Let's build X" → hyperpowers:brainstorming first'), no Skill tool_use.
